description: Data model for the family tree application, reflecting the actual EF Core models and API DTOs (FamilyTree-BackEnd/FamilyTree.Api/Models and Dtos). Each top-level key is a table/entity. Field 'type' values are logical types (map to .NET / DB types as appropriate). Keep this in sync whenever a model or DTO changes — it's the contract the frontend's src/api/types.ts is written against.

Person.description: A single family member. Source: Models/Person.cs, Dtos/PersonDto.cs.

Id.description: Auto-incrementing primary key. Present on PersonDto (API responses); omitted from PersonRequest (create/update request body).

BirthLastName.description: Surname at birth, if different from current LastName (e.g. maiden name after marriage). Useful for tracing lineage through name changes.

Gender.description: Used for display purposes (icons/pronouns) in the tree UI. Not used to constrain Parent1/Parent2, which are gender-neutral. Serialized as a string (JsonStringEnumConverter is registered globally).

BirthDate.description: Optional because exact birth dates for older ancestors are often unknown. .NET type is DateOnly.

DateOfDeath.description: Absence does not necessarily mean the person is alive; it may simply be unrecorded. .NET type is DateOnly.

PictureUrl.description: Single profile picture for v1 — a pasted URL, not an uploaded file. There is no image upload/storage in this app.

Biography.description: Free-form notes about the person (occupation, life story, anecdotes, etc.).

Parent1Id.description: Gender-neutral parent reference. No ordering/meaning implied between Parent1 and Parent2.

CreatedAt.description: Audit timestamp, set on insert. Present on PersonDto; omitted from PersonRequest.

UpdatedAt.description: Audit timestamp, set on insert and every update. Present on PersonDto; omitted from PersonRequest.

notes: There is no CreatedByUserId or any other audit-of-who field on this entity — records aren't attributed to the account that created them.
PersonRequest (used for both POST and PUT bodies) has the same shape as PersonDto minus Id, CreatedAt, and UpdatedAt.

Relationship.description: Represents a partnership/marriage between two people. Modeled as its own entity (rather than a single Partner field on Person) so a person can have multiple relationships over their lifetime (e.g. divorce and remarriage), each with its own dates and status. Source: Models/Relationship.cs, Dtos/RelationshipDto.cs.

Id.description: Present on RelationshipDto; omitted from RelationshipRequest.

Type.description: Current/final status of this relationship. Serialized as a string.

StartDate.description: e.g. marriage date or start of partnership. .NET type is DateOnly.

EndDate.description: e.g. divorce date, or date of a partner's death. .NET type is DateOnly.

CreatedAt.description: Present on RelationshipDto; omitted from RelationshipRequest.

UpdatedAt.description: Present on RelationshipDto; omitted from RelationshipRequest.

notes: There is no CreatedByUserId on this entity either.
RelationshipRequest (used for both POST and PUT bodies) has the same shape as RelationshipDto minus Id, CreatedAt, and UpdatedAt.

User.description: A login account used purely to gate write access to the tree — not a family-tree entity itself, and not exposed by any GET endpoint. Source: Models/User.cs, Dtos/AuthDtos.cs. This shape is simpler than earlier design drafts: no email, display name, role enum, or link to a Person record.

Username.description: Login identifier. There is no Id, Email, or DisplayName field — Username is effectively the primary key EF Core uses for lookups (see Data/Configurations/UserConfiguration.cs for the actual key mapping).

IsAdmin.description: Only true for accounts allowed to call POST /api/auth/users (create new accounts). This is a flat boolean, not a Role enum — there is no separate Editor/Viewer tier. Any authenticated user (admin or not) can create/edit/delete People and Relationships; the only thing IsAdmin gates is creating new User accounts.

notes: Login is by Username + Password (POST /api/auth/login), not email.

There is no self-service sign-up. New accounts are created by an existing admin via POST /api/auth/users (RequireAuthorization("AdminOnly")), or by inserting a row directly in the database for the very first account.
New accounts created via the API always have IsAdmin = false; promoting to admin currently requires a direct database update.
A successful login returns a JWT (LoginResponse: Token, ExpiresAt) carrying an "IsAdmin" claim ("true"/"false") that the AdminOnly authorization policy checks.
Children are derived by querying Person rows where Parent1Id or Parent2Id matches a given Person.Id — no separate 'Child' table is needed.
A person's partner(s) are derived by querying Relationship rows where Person1Id or Person2Id matches a given Person.Id.

All mutating endpoints (POST/PUT/DELETE on /api/people and /api/relationships, and POST /api/auth/users) require a valid JWT via RequireAuthorization(); GET endpoints on people/relationships are public.
Frontend TypeScript types mirroring these DTOs live in FamilyTree-FrontEnd/src/api/types.ts — update both together.

Deferred for later iterations: multiple photos per person (Photo gallery entity), adoptive/step/biological distinction on parent links, partial/approximate date precision (e.g. 'circa 1920'), privacy flags for living persons, audit-of-who-created-a-record.
